newsitem.title: PERU: Peru to auction Yauricocha mine September 15.
newsitem.headline: Peru to auction Yauricocha mine September 15.

text.p: Peru's state miner Centromin said Wednesday it would auction rights to its Yauricocha mine on September 15 as part of its piecemeal privatization program.

A Centromin statement said Yauricocha's minimum bid price had been fixed at $5 million, while the winning company would also be required to invest $2 million in the exploration phase and $7 million over five years if it takes up the option.
"The mode used will be the Transfer Option, under which the winning bidder will initially have the right to explore and study the concessions during a maximum period of two years," Centromin said.
"Upon completion of this period, or earlier if the investor wishes, he will decide whether to exercise the option and obtain the definitive transfer of all the assets."
The Yauricocha sale was postponed last year after the government failed to attract potential buyers for the unit despite lowering an original minimum bid price 15 percent to $8.5 million.
The polymetallic mine lies 220 miles (350 km) southeast of Lima and has proven and probable reserves of 2.8 million tonnes and potential reserves of six million tonnes.
